title: Special initial conditions often make one cellular automaton emulate another

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Special initial conditions often make one cellular automaton emulate another

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: It is common for a cellular automaton to have special initial conditions under which it behaves exactly like some other cellular automaton; for example rule 126 behaves like rule 90 when started from paired-cell blocks, and class 3 rules can thereby act like class 2 rules.

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: it turns out to be quite common for there to exist special initial conditions for one cellular automaton that make it behave just like some other cellular automaton.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 6, “Starting from Randomness”; section “Special Initial Conditions” (from p. 266), p. 269. Scope: cellular automata and their block emulations

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch06-18: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.77

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Individual block emulations are exact and readily verified using existing rule definitions. Their claimed prevalence is only measurable relative to bounded encoding choices.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Enumerate block encodings up to a fixed width for cellular-automaton pairs and verify the commuting relation between encoded evolution and the emulated rule. Report the proportion of source rules with at least one nontrivial emulation and reproduce the rule 126-to-90 example.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
“Common” requires a measure over rules and encodings.

Unbounded block widths cannot be exhaustively searched.

Trivial encodings must be excluded explicitly.

fields.value:

data adequacy: 0.58

operationalizability: 0.7

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The rule 126 emulation of rule 90 on blocks of paired cells is a finite case check and is decisive for that example. Quite common, and the further remark that class 3 rules can thereby act like class 2 rules, requires a survey whose hit rate depends on the encoding search. The example is resolvable now; the frequency claim is a sample.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Verify that every pair of aligned two-cell blocks under rule 126 updates, on alternate steps, exactly as rule 90 updates single cells, and search a declared family for further block emulations. A mismatch refutes the named example; the frequency claim depends on how often such encodings appear in the search.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The rule 126 example is a finite check and does not establish the frequency.

Behave exactly like must be a commuting diagram, not a visual resemblance.

Quite common needs a declared search over rules and block encodings.

fields.label: Dimension scores

data existence: 0.88
